The flat was beautiful. The price looked fair. Then I made one phone call.

If you are about to buy a home over ₹3 Crore in South Mumbai, read this short article before you sign anything.

South Bombay, from the towers that are selling right now.
by Nikhil Bora
October 21, 2026 | 9:40 AM IST

BuyerSide only
SoBo& beyond

The flat was genuinely beautiful. High floor, sea on two sides, a price that looked fair on paper. My client was ready to pay the token the next morning. He only called me to say thank you, not to ask.

So I asked him three questions. What did the two flats that sold in that tower last quarter actually go for. What was wrong with the stack he had picked. And did he know the builder was holding a quieter inventory list he had never been shown.

There was a long pause on the line. He did not know any of it. Nobody had told him. His broker had no reason to.

The broker is paid by the seller. The more you pay, the more he makes. That is not a scandal. It is just the math of the table you have been sitting at.

I have watched this happen for ten years. You get shown six flats a broker wants to move. You hear why each one is a once in a decade opportunity. And then you negotiate, alone, against a person who knows the real number and has every reason not to tell you.

None of it is loud. The flaws stay hidden until after the token. The comparable sales that would protect you never come up. Your budget, the one number you should guard with your life, is the first thing the broker learns and the last thing he forgets.

It is quiet, and it costs people lakhs. Sometimes a whole floor of a view they overpaid for. And they only feel it years later, when they try to sell.

Why I only ever work for the buyer

About eight years ago I stopped representing sellers entirely. One client at a time, on their side of the table, paid to protect their money and nothing else. No builder list to push. No commission that grows when you overpay. Here is the whole difference, side by side.
